title: The Eye Movement Your Mirror Shows—but You Normally Miss
titleSupport: Conditional title only if live Page composer provides field
description:
Try the mirror experiment: look from one eye to the other. Why can't you normally catch your eyes moving?

The reflection stays continuous. During rapid eye turns, visual sensitivity drops, and the clear views before and after can mask the blur. Watching a recording later separates that movement from your own eye turn.

Original illustrative animation; eye motion shown slowed. Synthetic narration; original synthesized sound.

Sources: Kleiser et al. (2004); Wurtz (2008, review); Diamond et al. (2000); Castet & Masson (2000).
